exposure: Maternal BMI (normal: 18.9-24.9 kg/m2, overweight: 25-29.9 kg/m2, obese: >30 kg/m2)
cohort: The study included 290 pregnant women who delivered at KIMS and RF, a tertiary care hospital in Amalapuram, Andhra Pradesh.
finding: Maternal obesity significantly increases the incidence of various maternal complications (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, postpartum hemorrhage, wound infections) and fetal complications (macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, NICU admissions, neonatal mortality).
mod_finding: Obese women exhibited significantly increased rates of cesarean sections (62.06%) compared to their counterparts.
cross-section timing: Data collected from July 2023 to June 2024
